I was sitting at my computer staring at a shopping cart full of things I don't really need when it occurred to me how much money I had been spending lately. then I realized that I've also been particularly proactive about my health/wellness - scheduled a doctor appointment, eye appointment, and mental health appointment. I called and fixed a mistaken charge for my medication from like a month ago. Somewhat ironically, I also impulsively spent money on completely paying off my credit card. I've also taken on a couple new hobbies.

I didn't run into debt or anything, but it's been a long time since I felt this manic. It worries me that it took me so long to notice. People don't really realize how difficult it is to be aware or both mania and depression initially, sometimes until it's too late. I've had a decent amount of success utilizing my mania instead of letting it guide my actions now that I'm aware of it.

I was pretty damned depressed for many months but recently started eating better and that led to exercising and starting to lose weight. I've been much less lazy than normal about everything. Your post makes me wonder if I'm not manic now. I hope not. I'd like to keep this train rolling.
I find that I am usually able to keep up, to some level or another, on healthy habits I fall into when I'm manic. It's the depression that kills it.

I have trouble differentiating between manic happiness and excitement and real happiness and excitement. I think part of the buying things while elevated is an attempt to compensate for lost time and neglected needs not addressed while depressed. The big red flag for me is when I'm physically unable to sleep. While coming down from my last mania, I bought a new computer desk and chair that I really could have used long time ago. To me, it sounds like you may just be taking care of needs neglected during depression. Enjoy the high, it's only a big problem when ones mood begins to interfere with functioning.

I think there's a balance. I probably choose to do the things, but the way I do them is what's influenced by the mania. Generally, though, the main signals for me are physiological. As such, it can be difficult for me to tell if I'm just happy. This episode is markedly more intense, though.

Over the years I kind of gave up trying to figure out if the mania was triggered or not. When I'm manic I'm more likely to go out and do things, or work on projects, or see things optimistically or confidently; especially compared to when I'm depressed. So I think that confounds things a lot. Given, though, that I have a fairly regular cycle, my assumption is that it is not triggered but that events will effect the strength of the episode. For example, recently I've had many good things happen to me.

I know for a fact that my depression can be triggered. When I get stressed out it really fucks me over. That's why I get so nervous about having a job. I recently got a position as a fill in person for a really relaxed local business, so that's been working out okay since it's only one or two or sometimes no days a week. And if I'm having a bad week I can just tell them I can't come in.
Your self-awareness while manic amazes me, granted it seems like this may have been going on for a bit. My manic states tend to go totally off the rails and I don't notice until it's far too late.
